title: Bhagvan Yadav @ Bhagvan Singh Yadav v. State of U.P. and others
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J. and Vivek Kumar Singh, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to clause 6.8.
headnote: A writ challenging a Tehsildar recovery citation and the licensee's recovery certificate in a matter of alleged theft and unauthorized use of electricity is not decided on the merits. The Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a self-contained code with a full-fledged mechanism; the consumer has an efficacious remedy to press relief under clause 6.8. The petition was disposed of with a week's time to take that recourse and a hope that the competent authority would proceed strictly in accordance with law. A later correction substituted 'file an appeal under provision' with 'press the relief under 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code'.
facts: Bhagvan Yadav challenged a Tehsildar recovery citation of 17 October 2021 (Kasimabad, Ghazipur) and an Executive Engineer, EDD-I, UPPCL, Ghazipur recovery certificate of 22 October 2020. The Corporation said the demand arose from theft and unauthorized use of electricity. A correction order of 12 May 2023 substituted, in the 2 January 2023 order, 'file an appeal under provision' with 'press the relief under 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code.'

holding_units.holding: Where a writ challenges a recovery citation and recovery certificate arising from alleged theft and unauthorized use of electricity, the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a self-contained code with a full-fledged mechanism. The consumer has an efficacious remedy to press relief under clause 6.8 (as later corrected from 'file an appeal') and is given a week's time to take that recourse; the writ is disposed of, the competent authority being expected to proceed strictly in accordance with law.

principle_tags.application: Writ against a recovery citation and certificate for alleged theft and unauthorized use was not examined on the merits; the petitioner was left to press relief under clause 6.8 within a week.
The Court treated the Supply Code as a self-contained mechanism and relegated the consumer to clause 6.8 rather than deciding the recovery.

not_decided.point: Merits of the recovery citation dated 17.10.2021 and the recovery certificate dated 22.10.2020
Whether the demand is governed by clause 6.8 (unauthorized use) or clauses 8.1–8.2 (theft)
not_decided.note: The Corporation and the Court treated theft and unauthorized use together under clause 6.8 without deciding any Chapter 8 overlay.
